problems: The blind guess (a long-necked wading bird) matches the figure reasonably well: a long vertical neck rises to the head, the wings spread out to both sides, and the tail hangs down. The figure reads as an upright bird.
The gold stick-figure lines carry most of the form. The blue contour wraps closely around them and is thin and sparse, so the figure reads more as a line drawing than a filled silhouette.

Key stars sit on plausible parts: crown (2081) and beak tip (2072) at the top, neck (2472) on the upper spine, body (3405) at the centre, elbow (5348) on the left wing, left wingtip (7588) far left, right wingtip (118234) far right, base of tail (2484) below the body, and the three tail tips (1599, 118121, 118322) at the bottom.
The labels collide: 'left tail feather tip' and 'right tail feather tip' overlap each other near the bottom, and 'left wingtip' sits on top of the wing line near the elbow label.
Two unlabelled stray stars at roughly (214,176) and (279,166) sit in the empty space above the left wing and add visual noise.
The right wing is a single straight line and the left wing is shorter and droops, so the wings are asymmetric and the bird's pose is harder to read.
output.advice: Keep the overall layout: head at top, tail at bottom, wings out to the sides. Improvements: (1) Move the label for 118121 (right tail feather tip) and 1599 (left tail feather tip) apart, or offset one to the right, so they no longer overlap. (2) Move the 'left wingtip' label off the wing line, for example below star 7588. (3) Fill or thicken the blue contour into a solid silhouette, and widen the body and wings so the figure reads as a bird rather than a stick figure. (4) Balance the wings: lengthen the left wing toward the same span as the right wing (7588 vs 118234) and keep the elbow 5348 on the wing's bend. (5) Remove or dim the two stray unlabelled stars near the top-left of the figure so they don't read as part of the drawing.
